## Well-definedness

To justify the conditional-kernel existence claim without assuming that the instance space is standard Borel, work on $\Omega=\mathsf X	imes\mathsf Y$ with law $P$, write $X(x,y)=x$ and $Y(x,y)=y$, and put $\mathcal G=\sigma(X)$. By [[thm-existence-of-regular-conditional-distributions-for-standard-borel-targets]], there is an everywhere probability kernel $L(\omega,dy)$ satisfying the conditional-event identities for the label coordinate given $\mathcal G$; the same theorem supplies a bimeasurable coding $c:\mathsf Y	o B$ onto a Borel set $B\subseteq[0,1]$. For each rational $q$, let $h_q(\omega)=L(\omega,c^{-1}(B\cap(-\infty,q]))$. Each $h_q$ is $\mathcal G$-measurable. Since $\mathcal G=\{X^{-1}(D):D\in\Sigma_X\}$ for an arbitrary measurable map $X$, choose $D_{q,r}\in\Sigma_X$ with $X^{-1}(D_{q,r})=\{h_q\le r\}$ for each rational $r\in[0,1]$, setting $D_{q,1}=\mathsf X$. These are countably many choices, available under AC. The functions $u_q(x)=\inf\{r\in\mathbb Q\cap[0,1]:x\in D_{q,r}\}$ are measurable because $\{u_q<a\}= igcup_{r\in\mathbb Q\cap[0,1],\ r<a}D_{q,r}$ for each real $a$, and they satisfy $u_q(X(\omega))=h_q(\omega)$ for every $\omega$.

On the range of $X$, the values $u_q$ are the rational CDF values of the pushforward of $L(\omega,\cdot)$ by $c$. Let $E_0$ consist of those $x$ for which $u_p(x)\le u_q(x)$ whenever rational $p<q$, $\lim_{n	o\infty}u_{-n}(x)=0$, $\lim_{n	o\infty}u_n(x)=1$, and $u_q(x)=\inf_{r\in\mathbb Q,\ r>q}u_r(x)$ for every rational $q$. These are countably many measurable conditions by [[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]], so $E_0$ is measurable and contains $X(\Omega)$. For $x\in E_0$, the function $F_x(t)=\inf_{q\in\mathbb Q,\ q>t}u_q(x)$ is a CDF and satisfies $F_x(q)=u_q(x)$ at rational $q$ by the right-limit condition; [[thm-probability-law-and-distribution-function-correspondence]] gives its unique Borel probability $
u_x$. For $x
otin E_0$, take $
u_x=\delta_0$. The evaluations $x\mapsto
u_x(( -\infty,t])$ are measurable by [[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]], and a Dynkin-system argument using [[thm-dynkin-pi-lambda]] extends measurability to every Borel set, so $x\mapsto
u_x$ is a probability kernel. For each $\omega$, uniqueness of the measure with the given rational CDF values gives $
u_{X(\omega)}=c_\#L(\omega,\cdot)$, hence $
u_{X(\omega)}(B)=1$. Thus $E=\{x:
u_x(B)=1\}$ is measurable and contains $X(\Omega)$. For $x\in E$ define $K(x,A)=

For all $\omega$ and $A\in\Sigma_Y$, $K(X(\omega),A)=L(\omega,A)$, so $K$ inherits the conditional-event identities from $L$.
